key_insight: Bottom-slope asymmetry changes the optimal initial balance of counter-propagating Rossby waves for finite-time growth, favoring the opposite amplitude bias to the exponentially growing normal mode.
engineering_relevance: The findings can inform stability analysis of rotating stratified flows, where normal-mode predictions alone may miss finite-time disturbance amplification.
method: Analyze two interacting Rossby waves in a sloped Eady model on an f-plane.
Control wave asymmetry through the bottom background potential-vorticity gradient.
Derive instantaneous-growth properties across a family of norms and examine finite-time optimal perturbations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports asymmetry-independent instantaneous-growth characteristics in the total-energy norm and analogous results in a Phillips model, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The proposed symmetry-based explanation remains speculative, and applicability beyond the idealized models is not established.
paper_title: Transient growth and Counter-propagating Rossby Waves in a sloped Eady problem
